target.title: fix(qa-lab): report authoritative Crabline readiness artifact
target.body:
Related: #105983

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA operators could be directed to the channel smoke artifact instead of Crabline's authoritative provider-readiness artifact when a generation returned distinct paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry `providerReadinessArtifactPath` through the QA artifact selection independently from `smokeArtifactPath`, while retaining the legacy completed-generation fallback for older Crabline results. The regression fixture uses distinct files so field swaps cannot pass unnoticed.

## User Impact

QA reports now identify the authoritative provider-readiness artifact without changing the existing smoke artifact recorded in summaries and evidence.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcwvd7j2rzzhk1b6dw4r4xx`: `pnpm test extensions/qa-lab/src/suite.test.ts` — 29 passed.
- Same Testbox: `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed.
- Fresh branch autoreview on `8a2da4b1bf1555fe0bfaf705eb57300c673c81be` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

target.title: fix(config): warn on JSON5 comment loss after successful config write
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105683

Fixes silent JSON5 comment loss when `openclaw.json` and its `$include`-referenced files are written back to disk. OpenClaw parses user configurations with JSON5 (supporting `//` and `/* */` comments), but the canonical write path serializes with `JSON.stringify`, which irreversibly strips all user-authored comments, documentation, and commented-out settings on every automatic config mutation.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Previous attempt (#105727) added a regex-based detector with a pre-commit warning. ClawSweeper review identified three defects:

1. **Incomplete JSON5 line continuation handling** — regex only recognized LF/CR/CRLF, missing U+2028/U+2029
2. **Warning emitted before write commit** — rejected writes still alarmed users
3. **[P1] Uncovered `$include` writer** — `writeRootBoundJsonFile` (single-file `$include` path) also stripped comments silently

This fix:
- Replaces the regex with a **character-by-character lexical scanner** covering all JSON5 escape sequences including U+2028/U+2029
- Warning fires only from `logConfigOverwrite()` (post-`replaceFileAtomic`)
- `onCommitted` callback in `writeRootBoundJsonFile` extends coverage to included files
- Recovery guidance points to the pre-write `.bak` backup

#### User Impact

- Users with comments in `openclaw.json` or included files (`plugins.json5`, etc.) see a post-commit warning
- Warning tells users to diff against the pre-write backup to recover comments
- False positives eliminated: URLs, `//` in strings, all JSON5 line-continued strings correctly ignored
- Plain JSON configs produce no warning

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Tests:**
  - `io.parse.test.ts` — 11 tests (+9: lexical scanner)
  - `io.write-config.test.ts` — 103 tests (no regression)
  - `io.audit.test.ts` — all tests (no regression)
  - `mutate.test.ts` — 46 tests (+1: include-file comment-loss warning)
- **Change scope:** 4 files, +230 lines
  - `src/config/io.ts` — +68: `hasJSON5Comments()` scanner + warning in `logConfigOverwrite` (root writer)
  - `src/config/mutate.ts` — +18: `onCommitted` callback in `writeRootBoundJsonFile` (include writer)
  - `src/config/io.parse.test.ts` — +57: 9 focused scanner tests
  - `src/config/mutate.test.ts` — +85: 1 focused include-writer test
  - No new dependencies, no config/CLI/SDK/docs/changelog surface
- **Both write paths covered:**
  - Root writer (`replaceFileAtomic`): warning in `logConfigOverwrite` post-commit
  - Include writer (`writeRootBoundJsonFile`): warning via `onCommitted` callback
- **Real behavior proof** — actual `writeConfigFile` call against a JSON5-commented config on real filesystem:

```

  Config Write — JSON5 Comment-Loss Warning Proof
====================================================================

[setup] /tmp/oc-proof-8BLZLn/.openclaw/openclaw.json
[setup] 317 bytes, 3 line comments, 1 block comment

[read]  hash=422ddd0dd094 valid=true size=317
  ✓ config file found
  ✓ raw has // line comments
  ✓ raw has /* */ block comments
  ✓ raw has inline // comment

[write] mutating config (adding plugins.entries.demo)...
[write] file on disk (256 bytes):
        | {
        |   "gateway": {
        |     "mode": "local",
        |     "port": 18789
        |   },
        |   "meta": {
        |     "lastTouchedVersion": "2026.7.2",
        |     "lastTouchedAt": "2026-07-13T05:53:03.623Z"
        |   },
        |   "plugins": {
        |     "entries": {
        |       "demo": {
        |         "enabled": true
        |       }
        |     }
        |   }
        | }

[check] comment-loss warning: PRESENT
[check]   Config write removed JSON5 comments from /tmp/oc-proof-8BLZLn/.openclaw/openclaw.json.
           A pre-write backup was saved to the config directory; diff it against the current
           file to recover commented-out settings.
  ✓ warning emitted after successful write
  ✓ warning names the config file
  ✓ warning tells user about backup
  ✓ written file is plain JSON (no //)
  ✓ written file is plain JSON (no /* */)
  ✓ new plugin entry persisted
  ✓ existing gateway config preserved

[check] backup: /tmp/oc-proof-8BLZLn/.openclaw/openclaw.json.bak
[check]   exists: true
[check]   317 bytes, has //: true, has /* */: true
  ✓ backup is byte-identical to original commented file
  ✓ pre-write backup exists at <config>.bak

[recovery] user can recover comments via:
[recovery]   cp /tmp/oc-proof-8BLZLn/.openclaw/openclaw.json.bak /tmp/oc-proof-8BLZLn/.openclaw/openclaw.json

====================================================================
  Passed: 13  |  Failed: 0
====================================================================
```

The proof script:
1. Writes a real `openclaw.json` with `//` line comments, `/* */` block comments, and `// inline` comments
2. Calls `createConfigIO().writeConfigFile()` to mutate the config (adding a plugin entry)
3. Confirms the warning fires after commit, the file is plain JSON, the `.bak` backup has identical commented content, and provides a recovery command
